afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KREV 140842
AFDREV

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
1242 AM PST Sat Nov 14 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* A travel window opens through Sunday, as clearing skies and dry 
  conditions return.

* A colder, weaker storm will likely bring snow to Sierra passes and 
  rain in the valleys late Sunday night into Monday.

* A stronger and colder storm Wednesday into Thursday could bring
  heavy Sierra snow and snow down to western Nevada valley floors.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

Sunday Afternoon - Sunday: 

* Expect a nice little break between storms today into Sunday. This 
  morning will start with cold morning lows in the teens and 20s, 
  with highs in the 40s and 50s. Sunday will warm even further, with 
  upper 40s in the Sierra and near 60 degrees in western Nevada. If 
  you need to cross the Sierra, this will be your best window, just 
  watch for lingering snow and slick spots on the roads. 

Sunday Night - Monday: 

* A fast-moving system arrives late Sunday into Monday morning.
  This will start with 50-65 mph ridge gusts Sunday night, when
  snow levels will be around 7000-8000 feet. Snow levels will then
  fall to around 5000-7000 feet (lower over the northern Sierra,
  higher along Mono County), before falling to 5000-5500 feet by
  Monday night. Carson Pass could see (75-95% chance) up to 6" of
  new snow, while Echo and Donner passes may see 2-4" or less.
  Mammoth may also see 2-4", while the Tahoe Basin may only see
  1-2" of new snow. Western Nevada may see another decent rain
  total, with a 70-80% chance to see 0.1" of rainfall. Plan on 
  winter driving on Monday morning, especially across the Sierra. 

Tuesday: 

* Cold morning start with teens in the Sierra and mid 20s in western 
  Nevada. There may be some lingering snow showers in the Tahoe 
  Basin. Tuesday afternoon will offer another brief Sierra traveling 
  break, with winds and snow returning by Wednesday. 

Wednesday - Thursday: 

* MORE SNOW! A colder system is expected to arrive midweek, with 
  exact timing still to be determined. Strong ridge winds will 
  increase to around 70+ mph Wednesday. Snow levels are appearing to 
  drop to valley floors by Thursday, which may impact commutes for 
  Reno-Carson City-Minden. We will work out snow totals as the 
  system draws nearer and the guidance finds more agreement. 

Next Friday: 

* The coldest air of the week looks to take aim for Thursday night 
  into Friday morning. Showers may linger into Friday, but things 
  look to dry out as we head into the weekend. HRICH

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast:  

*  Saturday will be quiet with VFR and light winds. Sunday, ridge 
   winds increase, bringing LLWS with ridge gusts to 50 mph.  

Regional Outlook: 

*  Skies will clear over the region for Saturday into Sunday. Sunday 
   ridge winds will increase, bringing areas of LLWS over the 
   Sierra. 

24-72 Hour Outlook: 

*  Saturday afternoon through Sunday offers the best flying
   conditions with VFR and lighter winds. The next storm brings
   snow and IFR conditions back over Sierra terminals late Sunday
   into Monday, while western Nevada airports will remain mostly
   VFR with brief morning MVFR due to rain showers. HRICH

&&

.REV Watches/Warnings/Advisories...
NV...Winter Storm Warning until 10 AM PST Saturday NVZ002.

CA...Winter Storm Warning until 10 AM PST Saturday CAZ072-073.

&&

$$

* CHANGES...None.

* WHAT...Snow. Additional snow accumulations up to one inch.

* WHERE...Mono County.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Lingering showers may continue to provide
light snow early this morning, but should taper off around or
before sunrise.
